dimensions.note: No credential or secret handling. Global args are paths and non-sensitive defaults; no vault refs needed.
All logging uses structured placeholders (Listed {count}, bd {method} failed (exit {code}: {detail})). No interpolation. Failures log at error, completions at info.

Four bare JSON.parse calls on bd stdout (lines 243, 291, 336, 409) throw a raw SyntaxError with no indication of which bd subcommand produced the unparseable output. runBdStrict already returns stdout; parsing should be wrapped so the error names the method. Non-blocking: bd --json is stable and every failure path already throws before writeResource.

Five tests cover the create/show/update/close round-trip, list and ready, truncation flagging, update arg validation, and CLI failure surfacing (exit code + stderr). Failure path is covered by a real nonexistent-ID call.

create is not idempotent: a re-run creates a second issue. bd has no --idempotency-key flag on create, so this cannot be fixed in the model without deduplicating on title via externalRef. close is idempotent (bd close on a closed issue succeeds) and update --claim is documented idempotent by bd. Non-blocking; documented rather than changed.

Verified against the live CLI: bd list/ready accept --limit (defaults 50 and 100 respectively), bd update accepts --claim/--title/-d/-s/-p/-a/--add-label/--remove-label, bd close accepts --reason. bd show --json wraps the record in a single-element array, which fetchIssue handles.
Deno.Command().output() fully drains and closes pipes on every call. No open handles, no temp files created by the model. The bd-usable check also uses output().
README examples use bd-123 placeholders and my-tracker. No real hostnames, IPs, or account identifiers in README, tests, or fixtures.
All schemas use z.object with no passthrough. IssueSchema is strict, so CEL expression validation works.
The single issue spec sets lifetime 30d and garbageCollection 10, appropriate for high-churn list/ready output.

No delete or sync method. Beads has no delete (closure is terminal) and the model is a live projection of the bd database, so sync is what list/ready already do. Intentional for this domain, not a gap.
The bd-usable check runs bd --version from bdDir and fails with the exit code and stderr, labeled dependency so mutating methods skip cleanly when the CLI is absent.
All six methods write spec issue with instance issue-<bd-id>. Unique per issue, no collisions, consistent shape across every writer.
No direct dataRepository access. update and close re-fetch through fetchIssue (bd show) rather than reading stale stored state, which is correct for a projection of an external CLI database.
An upgrades entry exists for every published version including 2026.10.02.3, each a no-op attribute passthrough since no global argument schema changed.

mechanical.schema-write-conformance: pass — IssueSchema has 13 fields; normalizeIssue writes all 13; closeIssue spreads the fetched issue and overrides only status and updatedAt. No placeholder writes.
mechanical.truncation-honesty: FIXED — list and ready capped at limit with no truncated field on the spec, and relied on bd's own default cap (50 for list, 100 for ready), so a limit of 200 would silently return 50. Added truncated to IssueSchema, set it on every returned issue, and pass --limit <limit+1> to bd so the flag reflects bd's real cap. Covered by a new test.
mechanical.instance-name-consistency: pass — all writers emit issue-<bd-id> against spec issue with identical schema shape.
mechanical.schema-field-coverage: pass — 13 of 13 schema fields written; the three count fields have code paths populating them from bd's dependency_count/dependent_count/comment_count.
